cases.title: Shadows Over Serenity Wing
cases.location: Serenity Wing, St. Lumina Medical Center
cases.incident_overview: Nurses in Serenity Wing reported Wi-Fi dropouts disrupting cardiac monitors. A clinician muttered, "The signal’s fading like a ghost." Connectivity faltered on the 5GHz band, stalling real-time patient data feeds during peak hours.
cases.investigation_breakdown: Using the Wi-Fi App on EtherScope nXG, I detected elevated noise levels on 5GHz channels 36–48. AirMapper App generated detailed heatmaps, revealing signal degradation near the wing’s imaging suite. Cross-referencing with Spectrum App, I identified non-802.11 interference spikes correlating with equipment activation times.
cases.root_cause: A malfunctioning MRI machine’s shielding had degraded, leaking RF interference into the 5GHz Wi-Fi spectrum, disrupting access points.
cases.resolution: Reconfigured APs to use unaffected channels (149–161) based on Wi-Fi App data. Coordinated with maintenance to repair the MRI’s shielding.
cases.summary: AirMapper and Wi-Fi Apps pinpointed MRI-induced interference. Channel reassignment and equipment repair ensured uninterrupted patient monitoring.

cases.title: The IP Thief of Horizon Admin
cases.location: Horizon Administrative Hub, Crescent Vale Hospital
cases.incident_overview: Admin staff in Horizon Hub couldn’t access electronic health records, with devices failing to obtain IP addresses. A sysadmin grumbled, "Something’s stealing our IPs." The issue paralyzed documentation during a busy shift.
cases.investigation_breakdown: AutoTest App revealed DHCP response failures, with devices receiving invalid IP offers. Discovery App mapped the network, identifying an unauthorized DHCP server broadcasting from a device in the staff lounge. Packet analysis showed the rogue server assigning IPs outside the hospital’s subnet, causing conflicts.
cases.root_cause: A misconfigured smart coffee maker, recently installed, was running an unauthorized DHCP service, clashing with the hospital’s primary DHCP server.
cases.resolution: Isolated the coffee maker using Discovery App’s topology view. Reconfigured the hospital’s DHCP server to enforce stricter lease policies and blocked unauthorized servers.
cases.summary: AutoTest and Discovery Apps exposed a rogue DHCP server in a smart device. Isolation and server hardening resolved the issue, restoring EHR access.

cases.title: The Wired Wraith of Eclipse ICU
cases.location: Eclipse Intensive Care Unit, Nova General Hospital
cases.incident_overview: ICU monitors in Eclipse Unit lagged, dropping critical alerts. A nurse snapped, "The cables are cursed." Ethernet links showed intermittent packet loss, risking delayed responses to patient emergencies.
cases.investigation_breakdown: LANBERT App tested the Cat6 cabling infrastructure, revealing intermittent signal degradation on a 2.5Gbps link to the ICU’s central switch. Bit-error rate tests showed errors spiking during high traffic. Physical inspection of the wiring closet uncovered a partially unplugged cable with frayed shielding.
cases.root_cause: A damaged Cat6 cable, loosened during recent maintenance, caused intermittent packet loss under heavy load, disrupting monitor connectivity.
cases.resolution: Replaced the faulty cable and retested with LANBERT App, confirming stable 2.5Gbps performance. Secured wiring closet to prevent future tampering.
cases.summary: LANBERT App identified a damaged cable causing packet loss. Replacement and securing infrastructure ensured reliable ICU monitoring.

cases.title: The Rogue Breach in Aurora Clinic
cases.location: Aurora Outpatient Clinic, Zenith Medical Complex
cases.incident_overview: An unknown SSID appeared in Aurora Clinic, raising alarms of a security breach. A guard hissed, "Someone’s hijacking our airwaves." Unauthorized Wi-Fi traffic threatened patient data confidentiality.
cases.investigation_breakdown: Spectrum App with NXT-2000 adapter detected a rogue AP on the 2.4GHz band, broadcasting a spoofed SSID mimicking the hospital’s. Capture App recorded packets, revealing connection attempts to a malicious server. Triangulation with Spectrum App localized the AP to a public waiting area.
cases.root_cause: A rogue access point, hidden in a waiting room power strip, was deployed to execute a man-in-the-middle attack, capturing credentials from unsuspecting users.
cases.resolution: Removed the rogue AP using Spectrum App’s localization data. Upgraded to WPA3 encryption and implemented MAC filtering to prevent future attacks.
cases.summary: Spectrum and Capture Apps uncovered a rogue AP orchestrating a credential theft attempt. Removal and enhanced security measures safeguarded patient data.

cases.title: The Data Choke in Radiant Imaging
cases.tool: EtherScope nXG (Path Analysis App, AutoTest App)
cases.location: Radiant Imaging Department, Solace Health Center
cases.incident_overview: Radiology imaging uploads in Radiant Department slowed to a crawl, delaying diagnoses. A tech cursed, "The network’s suffocating." High latency and packet loss plagued the wired path to the imaging server.
cases.investigation_breakdown: Path Analysis App traced the network path from the radiology workstation to the server, identifying a switch port with 80ms latency spikes. AutoTest App confirmed throughput drops to 10Mbps on a 1Gbps link. Switch logs revealed QoS misconfiguration prioritizing non-critical traffic.
cases.root_cause: A switch port’s QoS settings were misconfigured, prioritizing guest Wi-Fi over critical imaging traffic, causing a bottleneck during peak usage.
cases.resolution: Reconfigured QoS to prioritize imaging traffic and retested with Path Analysis App, achieving sub-10ms latency and full 1Gbps throughput.
cases.summary: Path Analysis and AutoTest Apps exposed a QoS misconfiguration throttling imaging traffic. Reconfiguration restored timely diagnostic workflows.

cases.title: The Silent Smartboards of Willow Creek
cases.location: Willow Creek Middle School, Classroom B-12
cases.incident_overview: Teachers reported smartboards freezing during lessons, disrupting student engagement. A frustrated educator snapped, "These boards are mute when we need them most." Wi-Fi on the 2.4GHz band was unstable, affecting classroom interactivity.
cases.investigation_breakdown: Using the Wi-Fi App on EtherScope nXG, I scanned the 2.4GHz band, detecting high channel utilization on channels 1, 6, and 11. AirMapper App’s heatmaps showed overlapping signals from adjacent classrooms. Analysis confirmed co-channel interference from nearby access points.
cases.root_cause: Overlapping Wi-Fi channels from neighboring classroom APs caused interference, degrading smartboard performance.
cases.resolution: Reconfigured APs to non-overlapping channels (1, 6, 11) using Wi-Fi App recommendations. Verified signal strength with AirMapper to ensure coverage.
cases.summary: Wi-Fi App and AirMapper resolved channel overlap, enabling seamless smartboard operation.

cases.title: The Ghostly Guest Network of Pineview Elementary
cases.incident_overview: Students accessed an unauthorized guest Wi-Fi network, bypassing school content filters. A librarian muttered, "Kids are on some rogue network!" The breach risked exposure to unfiltered content during recess.
cases.investigation_breakdown: Spectrum App detected a non-802.11 signal broadcasting a suspicious SSID, "Pineview_Guest," on the 2.4GHz band. Capture App recorded packets, revealing the rogue AP’s MAC address and connection attempts to an external server. Triangulation localized the AP to the cafeteria.
cases.root_cause: A rogue access point, hidden in a cafeteria vending machine, broadcast a fake guest SSID to bypass school security.
cases.resolution: Removed the rogue AP using Spectrum App’s localization. Implemented MAC address filtering and updated SSID authentication to WPA3.
cases.summary: Spectrum and Capture Apps identified and eliminated a rogue AP, securing the school’s Wi-Fi.

cases.title: The Stalled Tablets of Oakridge High
cases.incident_overview: Tablets used for state testing failed to connect, showing "No IP address" errors. A proctor groaned, "We’re losing time!" The issue threatened to delay critical assessments.
cases.investigation_breakdown: AutoTest App identified DHCP request failures, with tablets receiving no IP offers. Discovery App mapped the network, revealing a DHCP server overload. Logs showed the DHCP scope had run out of available addresses due to excessive device connections.
cases.root_cause: A misconfigured DHCP scope with a limited address pool was exhausted by concurrent tablet connections.
cases.resolution: Expanded the DHCP scope using Discovery App’s network map. Configured lease timeouts to recycle IPs faster, verified with AutoTest.
cases.summary: AutoTest and Discovery Apps resolved DHCP exhaustion, ensuring tablet connectivity for exams.

cases.title: The Wired Whispers of Maple Grove
cases.location: Maple Grove Junior High, Computer Lab
cases.incident_overview: Wired classroom computers lagged during online assessments, frustrating students. A teacher sighed, "The network’s whispering, not working." Ethernet connections showed intermittent delays.
cases.investigation_breakdown: LANBERT App tested Cat5e cabling, detecting high packet loss on a 1Gbps link to the lab’s switch. Bit-error rate tests pinpointed a faulty port. Inspection revealed a corroded switch port connector.
cases.root_cause: A faulty Ethernet switch port caused packet loss, slowing computer lab connectivity.
cases.resolution: Replaced the switch port and retested with LANBERT App, confirming stable 1Gbps performance. Secured cabling to prevent future issues.
cases.summary: LANBERT App identified a faulty switch port, restoring lab connectivity.

cases.title: The Bandwidth Bottleneck of Cedar Lane
cases.tool: EtherScope nXG (Path Analysis App, AutoTest App)
cases.incident_overview: Video lessons in a digital classroom buffered endlessly, halting instruction. A student complained, "The videos are stuck!" High latency disrupted e-learning.
cases.investigation_breakdown: Path Analysis App traced the path from classroom devices to the server, identifying a 100ms latency spike at a core switch. AutoTest App confirmed throughput drops to 5Mbps on a 100Mbps link. Switch logs revealed a QoS policy prioritizing non-educational traffic.
cases.root_cause: A misconfigured QoS policy throttled educational traffic, prioritizing guest Wi-Fi.
cases.resolution: Reconfigured QoS to prioritize classroom traffic, verified with Path Analysis App for sub-10ms latency and 100Mbps throughput.
cases.summary: Path Analysis and AutoTest Apps resolved a QoS bottleneck, ensuring smooth video lessons.

cases.title: The Vanishing VLANs of Sterling Hall
cases.incident_overview: Dormitory Wi-Fi dropped, isolating students from e-learning platforms. A resident advisor grumbled, "The network’s vanished!" Devices failed to connect to the student VLAN.
cases.investigation_breakdown: NetTag App scanned VLAN configurations, revealing missing VLAN assignments on the dormitory switch. AutoTest App confirmed no DHCP responses on the student subnet. Logs showed a recent switch update had erased VLAN settings.
cases.root_cause: A switch misconfiguration during an update deleted student VLAN assignments.
cases.resolution: Restored VLAN configurations using NetTag App’s topology data. Validated connectivity with AutoTest App.
cases.summary: NetTag and AutoTest Apps fixed VLAN misconfigurations, reconnecting students.

cases.title: The Rogue Streamer of Campus Commons
cases.location: Campus Commons Lecture Hall, Crestwood University
cases.incident_overview: Lecture hall Wi-Fi slowed, disrupting hybrid classes. A professor snapped, "The network’s crawling!" Students couldn’t stream live lectures.
cases.investigation_breakdown: Discovery App mapped the network, identifying a high-bandwidth device in the lecture hall. Capture App analyzed traffic, revealing a student’s unauthorized streaming server consuming 50Mbps. The device was traced to a lecture hall outlet.
cases.root_cause: A student’s unauthorized streaming server hogged bandwidth, slowing Wi-Fi.
cases.resolution: Blocked the device using Discovery App’s MAC address. Implemented bandwidth caps for non-academic devices.
cases.summary: Discovery and Capture Apps stopped a rogue streaming server, restoring lecture connectivity.

cases.title: The Echoes of Emerson Library
cases.incident_overview: Wi-Fi in the library fluctuated, hindering research access. A student whispered, "The signal’s fading in and out." Connectivity on the 5GHz band was inconsistent.
cases.investigation_breakdown: Spectrum App detected non-Wi-Fi interference on 5GHz channels 36–48. AirMapper App’s heatmaps showed signal drops near a study lounge. Interference spikes correlated with a nearby microwave oven’s operation.
cases.root_cause: A microwave oven’s RF leakage interfered with the 5GHz Wi-Fi spectrum.
cases.resolution: Relocated the microwave and reconfigured APs to unaffected channels (149–161) using Spectrum App data.
cases.summary: Spectrum and AirMapper Apps eliminated microwave interference, ensuring reliable research access.

cases.title: The Frozen Portals of Tech Tower
cases.tool: EtherScope nXG (Path Analysis App, AutoTest App)
cases.location: Tech Tower Computer Lab, Bayside University
cases.incident_overview: Wired lab computers failed to access cloud-based IDEs, stalling coding projects. A student cursed, "The portals are frozen!" Outbound traffic was blocked.
cases.investigation_breakdown: Path Analysis App traced the path to the cloud server, identifying a firewall blocking port 443. AutoTest App confirmed no connectivity beyond the campus gateway. Firewall logs revealed a new rule mistakenly blocking HTTPS traffic.
cases.root_cause: A misconfigured firewall rule blocked outbound HTTPS traffic.
cases.resolution: Corrected the firewall rule and retested with Path Analysis App, confirming full connectivity.
cases.summary: Path Analysis and AutoTest Apps fixed a firewall misconfiguration, enabling cloud access.

cases.title: The Shadow SSID of Union Plaza
cases.incident_overview: A fake university SSID appeared in Union Plaza, tricking students into sharing credentials. A security officer hissed, "We’ve got a shadow network!" The breach risked data theft.
cases.investigation_breakdown: Spectrum App detected a rogue AP broadcasting "Hillcrest_FreeWiFi" on the 2.4GHz band. Capture App recorded packets, showing phishing attempts to a malicious server. Triangulation localized the AP to a plaza bench.
cases.root_cause: A rogue access point, hidden in a public charger, conducted a phishing attack via a fake SSID.
cases.resolution: Removed the rogue AP using Spectrum App’s localization. Deployed WPA3 and educated students on SSID verification.
cases.summary: Spectrum and Capture Apps stopped a phishing AP, protecting student data.
